claims.text: A conformal 1–2 nm ALD-deposited CeO₂ overcoat on alumina-supported Pt will improve catalytic activity under automotive exhaust conditions.
The CeO₂ overcoat will improve catalyst durability under automotive exhaust conditions.
The CeO₂ overcoat will enable reduced platinum-group-metal loading.
ALD can produce a nanoscale CeO₂ shell that encapsulates individual Pt nanoparticles without fully blocking their active sites.
The CeO₂ overcoat enhances oxygen-storage capacity.
The CeO₂ overcoat acts as a physical barrier against Pt sintering during high-temperature redox cycling.
Enhanced oxygen storage and reduced Pt sintering preserve high catalytic activity at lower overall Pt loading.
Relative to an untreated catalyst, the ALD-treated catalyst will have a lower pollutant-conversion light-off temperature.
Relative to an untreated catalyst, the ALD-treated catalyst will have a higher turnover frequency for pollutant conversion.
Relative to an untreated catalyst, the ALD-treated catalyst will undergo less Pt nanoparticle sintering after repeated thermal cycling.
The predicted improvements require the CeO₂ overcoat to be uniformly deposited and precisely controlled to a thickness of 1–2 nm.
An excessively thick or nonuniform CeO₂ overcoat may block active sites.
An insufficient or nonuniform CeO₂ overcoat may provide inadequate resistance to Pt sintering.
The proposed mechanism may not hold outside typical automotive exhaust temperature and redox conditions.
